judgment.rationale: The report is too underspecified to establish a root cause, but the comments and logs indicate random deactivation and possible character-triggered process termination. The PowerAccent interface launches a child process without proving the failing event, so focused evidence collection is required before implementation.
judgment.recommended_action: Capture one reproducible deactivation with a fresh diagnostic report and the exact character/input sequence, then trace child-process exit and relaunch handling.

evidence.fact: The issue body provides only "use quick accent"; comments indicate some characters may kill the process and logs show disable/relaunch activity without an error signature.
PowerAccentModuleInterface enable launches PowerToys.PowerAccent.exe; disable signals exit, waits, may terminate, and closes the process handle.
No confirmed public fix or exact reproduction sequence was identified.

fix_assessment.rationale: A child-process lifecycle fix is plausible but not safe to implement without separating user-triggered disable, crash, and input-triggered termination.

proposed_fixes.title: Harden Quick Accent child-process lifecycle handling
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The interface may treat an unexpected PowerToys.PowerAccent.exe exit or shutdown race as a normal disable, but the triggering condition is unconfirmed.
plan: Record process exit reason and the initiating enable/disable transition with public-safe diagnostics.
Reproduce the reported character matrix and identify whether input causes termination or only exposes a lifecycle race.
Make relaunch/state reconciliation explicit without relaunching after an intentional user disable.
verification: The original character/input sequence is stable across repeated runs.
Unexpected exits recover or surface a clear error without silently flipping the feature off.

confidence.rationale: The current evidence is insufficient to choose a safe lifecycle change.

issue_context.summary: Quick Accent sometimes deactivates without an intentional user action; the available evidence suggests a process-lifecycle or input-triggered failure but does not identify which.
known_information: The issue lacks a concrete sequence, affected character set, and fresh diagnostic report tied to one occurrence.
The module interface owns child-process launch and shutdown.
Existing logs show disable/relaunch but no confirmed error signature.
inferences: The failure may be caused by a child process exit that the interface does not distinguish from an intentional disable.
Character-specific input may be relevant, but this is not confirmed.
issue_context.analysis: Instrument the child-process lifecycle and reproduce with a minimal character matrix before changing relaunch policy.

information_gaps.information: The exact character/input sequence, whether the PowerAccent process exits or the setting flips, and the time of one occurrence.
information_gaps.why_needed: These facts distinguish input handling from process supervision and settings persistence.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce once, note the character sequence and time, and run /bugreport immediately after the deactivation.

actions.label: Request targeted evidence
actions.note: Separate process exit from settings-state changes before implementation.

comment.body: The current report says Quick Accent deactivates, and the available logs show disable/relaunch activity but no confirmed error. Please provide one exact reproduction: the trigger character or key sequence, whether the PowerAccent window/process disappears, whether the Settings toggle changes, and the approximate time. Reproduce once on the current build and run /bugreport immediately afterward. This targeted sequence will distinguish input handling, child-process exit, and settings persistence without requiring private logs in the issue body.

actions.label: Approve focused fix design
actions.note: The proposed design is specific enough for fork-side implementation after maintainer approval.

design.scope: Add minimal child-process lifecycle diagnostics and correct only the confirmed exit/relaunch or input path.
acceptance_criteria: An unexpected child-process exit is distinguishable from intentional disable.
The reported character sequence no longer deactivates Quick Accent.
Intentional disable still shuts down promptly without an unwanted relaunch.
